claim: Apical constriction is a basic mechanism for epithelial morphogenesis that makes columnar cells into wedge shape and bends a flat cell sheet.
source: Apical constriction is a basic mechanism for epithelial morphogenesis, making columnar cells into wedge shape and bending a flat cell sheet.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract describing the general understanding of apical constriction.

claim: It has long been thought that apically localized myosin generates a contractile force and drives cell deformation during apical constriction.
source: It has long been thought that an apically localized myosin generates a contractile force and drives the cell deformation.
evidence: This statement references the conventional model in the field.

claim: When increased apical surface contractility was tested in a cellular Potts model simulation, the constriction increased pressure inside the cell and pushed its lateral surface outward, making cells adopt a drop shape instead of wedge shape.
source: However, when we tested the increased apical surface contractility in a cellular Potts model simulation, the constriction increased pressure inside the cell and pushed its lateral surface outward, making the cells adopt a drop shape instead of the expected wedge shape.
evidence: This is a direct result from the authors' simulation experiments.

claim: An alternative model in which cell shape is determined by cell membrane elasticity and endocytosis, with increased pressure balanced among cells, can keep the lateral surface straight.
source: To keep the lateral surface straight, we considered an alternative model in which the cell shape was determined by cell membrane elasticity and endocytosis, and the increased pressure is balanced among the cells.
evidence: This describes the authors' proposed alternative model.

claim: The cellular Potts model simulation with the alternative model succeeded in reproducing apical constriction.
source: The cellular Potts model simulation succeeded in reproducing the apical constriction
evidence: This is a result from the authors' simulations.

claim: Too strong apical surface tension might prevent tissue invagination.
source: it also suggested that a too strong apical surface tension might prevent the tissue invagination.
evidence: This is a suggestion from the simulation results.

claim: Non-muscle myosin II crosslinks and contracts the actin filament network during apical constriction.
source: Studies in genetics and molecular biology had revealed an involvement of the motor protein non-muscle myosin II which crosslinks and contracts the actin filament network.
evidence: This references established findings from genetics and molecular biology studies.

claim: The actomyosin network is formed beneath the cell apical surface (cortical actomyosin) and lining apical-lateral cell-cell interface (circumferential actomyosin).
source: The actomyosin network is formed beneath the cell apical surface (cortical actomyosin) and lining apical-lateral cell-cell interface (circumferential actomyosin), linked with adherens junctions and tight junctions so that it makes a supracellular continuous structure (Martin et al., 2010; Takeichi, 2014).
evidence: This describes the localization of actomyosin networks with supporting citations.

claim: In Drosophila melanogaster mesoderm invagination, ventral cells express transcription factors Twist and Snail which induce expression of genes including regulators of actin and myosin.
source: In Drosophila melanogaster mesoderm invagination, ventral cells express transcription factors Twist and Snail which then induce expression of numerous genes including regulators of the actin and myosin, such as T48, Fog, Mist, RhoGEF2, Rho, and Rock (Martin, 2020).
evidence: This describes a known molecular pathway with citation.

claim: Down-regulation of myosin regulators impaired the localization and activation of myosin and delayed or prevented apical constriction.
source: while down-regulation of those regulators impaired the localization and activation of the myosin, and delayed or prevented the apical constriction (Dawes-Hoang et al., 2005; Xie et al., 2016; Kölsch et al., 2007; Mason et al., 2013).
evidence: This summarizes findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Similar regulation of myosin by Rho and Rock was found responsible for apical constriction in other organs and other insects.
source: Similar regulation of the myosin by Rho and Rock was found responsible for the apical constriction in other organs (Brodu and Casanova, 2006; Chung et al., 2017; Guru et al., 2022; Manning et al., 2013; Röper, 2012) and other insects (Münster et al., 2019; Benton et al., 2019; Urbansky et al., 2016).
evidence: This generalizes findings across different biological contexts with citations.

claim: In vertebrates, cortical myosin was not observed but circumferential myosin was enriched and recruited together with Rock by PDZ domain containing protein Shroom 3.
source: In vertebrates, the cortical myosin was not observed but the circumferential myosin was enriched, recruited together with Rock by PDZ domain containing protein Shroom 3, which was also found responsible for the apical constriction (Nishimura and Takeichi, 2008; Lang et al., 2014; Plageman et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2007; Chung et al., 2010; McGreevy et al., 2015; Haigo et al., 2003; Hildebrand, 2005).
evidence: This describes vertebrate-specific mechanisms with multiple citations.

claim: The myosin-based model was validated by simulations with finite element model or vertex model.
source: The myosin-based model was validated by simulations (Rauzi et al., 2013) with finite element model (Conte et al., 2012; Perez-Mockus et al., 2017) or vertex model (Sherrard et al., 2010; Polyakov et al., 2014; Inoue et al., 2016; Pérez-González et al., 2021).
evidence: This references prior simulation studies that validated the conventional model.

claim: In finite element model simulations, a cell was represented by few quadrilateral elements and its cytosol was assumed to be viscous.
source: In the finite element model, a cell was represented by few quadrilateral elements and its cytosol was assumed to be viscous.
evidence: This describes the methodology of finite element modeling.

claim: Finite element model studies showed that the surface tension of invaginated cells was more influential than those of surrounding cells.
source: The forces were varied in the simulation to show that the surface tension of the invaginated cells was more influential than those of surrounding cells, and that the invagination was robust against the variance in the force.
evidence: This summarizes findings from finite element model studies.

claim: Vertex model studies succeeded in reproducing apical constriction by increased apical surface tension.
source: These studies succeeded in reproducing the apical constriction by the increased apical surface tension
evidence: This summarizes results from vertex model studies.

claim: Actomyosin was localized to boundaries between amnioserosa and lateral epidermis or neural plate and epidermal ectoderm.
source: For example, actomyosin was localized to a boundary between amnioserosa and lateral epidermis (Hutson et al., 2003; Hayes and Solon, 2017) or neural plate and epidermal ectoderm (Hashimoto et al., 2015; Galea et al., 2017; Galea et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes observed localization patterns with citations.

claim: Supracellular myosin cables were found encircling salivary glands and tracheal pit during their invagination.
source: Similar supracellular myosin cables were found encircling salivary glands (Röper, 2012; Chung et al., 2017) and tracheal pit (Nishimura et al., 2007; Ogura et al., 2018) during their invagination.
evidence: This describes observed structures with citations.

claim: Planar compression was proposed to be able to drive epithelial folding.
source: Also, a planar compression was proposed to be able to drive the epithelial folding (Hočevar Brezavšček et al., 2012).
evidence: This references a proposed mechanism with citation.

claim: In the cellular Potts model simulations with increased apical surface contractility, cells with increased contractility were covered by surrounding cells and delaminated one by one from edges.
source: In contrast to the simulations in the preceding studies (Sherrard et al., 2010; Conte et al., 2012; Perez-Mockus et al., 2017; Pérez-González et al., 2021), our simulations could not reproduce the apical constriction, but cells with the increased apical surface contractility were covered by surrounding cells and delaminated one by one from edges (Figure 2a, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is a direct result from the authors' simulations shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Including surface elasticity kept cells' surface perimeter in a narrower range but cells were still delaminated.
source: To prevent the surface expansion, we included the surface elasticity term (Equation 2). It kept the cells surface perimeter in a narrower range as expected, but still the center cells were delaminated and adopted similar shapes (Figure 2b).
evidence: This describes simulation results shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Simulations of the supracellular myosin cable without increased apical surface contractility resulted in center cells being covered and delaminated.
source: We also simulated deformation with the supracellular myosin cable but without the increased apical surface contractility. In the cross section, the shrinkage of the circular supracellular myosin cable was simulated with a move of adherens junction under the myosin cable toward the midline. Either with or without the surface elasticity, the center cells were covered by the pulled cells and delaminated (Figure 2c).
evidence: This describes simulation results shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The increased apical surface contractility and the supracellular myosin cable cannot drive the apical constriction.
source: These results suggest that the increased apical surface contractility and the supracellular myosin cable cannot drive the apical constriction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the simulation results.

claim: Early deformation in the cellular Potts model was characterized by only the edge cell shrinking its apical surface, inner cells remaining columnar, and the edge cell's lateral surface curving outward.
source: To investigate the origin of the difference between the vertex model and the cellular Potts model results, we first looked into an early deformation of the cells in the cellular Potts model (Figure 3a and b). It was characterized by (1) that only the edge cell shrank its apical surface, (2) that inner cells remained in the columnar shape, and (3) that a lateral surface of the edge cell was curved outward.
evidence: This describes observations from the cellular Potts model simulations shown in Figure 3.

claim: A practical pulling force on the cell-cell junction by cell apical surfaces remained only on the edge of cells with increased apical surface contractility.
source: Then, a practical pulling force on the cell-cell junction by the cell apical surfaces remained only on the edge of the cells with the increased apical surface contractility (Figure 3c–e).
evidence: This is an inference from the model analysis illustrated in Figure 3c-e.

claim: The edge cell shrank its apical surface and consequently decreased its volume, increasing internal pressure due to cell volume conservation.
source: The edge cell shrank its apical surface and consequently decreased its volume. The decrease in the volume increased the internal pressure due to the cell volume conservation, and a difference in the pressure between the contracting and non-contracting cells resulted in the lateral surface curvature.
evidence: This is an inference from the model behavior.

claim: The difference between vertex model and cellular Potts model results was due to the straight lateral surface imposed on the vertex model.
source: These results indicate that the difference between the vertex model and the cellular Potts model results was due to the straight lateral surface imposed on the vertex model, a restriction that seems not natural for epithelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the energy analysis comparing the two models.

claim: The cellular Potts model simulation with increased apical surface contractility reproduced a phenotype of endocytosis down-regulation.
source: Also, we expect that the cellular Potts model simulation with the increased apical surface contractility reproduced a phenotype of endocytosis down-regulation as discussed later.
evidence: This is a speculation by the authors to be discussed later.

claim: Apical constriction requires a mechanism to simultaneously shrink the apical surface among cells in a cluster and a mechanism to keep the lateral surface straight.
source: Since the cellular Potts model simulation indicated that the increased apical surface contractility could not drive the apical constriction, we revisited requirements for the apical constriction. It requires (1) a mechanism to simultaneously shrink the apical surface among cells in a cluster, and (2) a mechanism to keep the lateral surface straight.
evidence: This is an inference from the simulation results.

claim: The simultaneous apical shrinkage will increase pressures in cells, but the increase will be synchronized and the pressure will be balanced.
source: Actually, the condition (2) can be satisfied when the condition (1) is achieved because the simultaneous apical shrinkage will increase the pressures in the cells, but the increase will also be synchronized and thus the pressure will be balanced.
evidence: This is a logical inference about pressure balance.

claim: The apical shrinkage can be synchronized when the energy function and its derivative are both increasing with respect to the apical width.
source: As suggested by the cell shape energy analysis (Figure 3f), the apical shrinkage can be synchronized when the energy function and its derivative are both increasing with respect to the apical width.
evidence: This is an inference from the energy analysis shown in Figure 3f.

claim: Simulations with decreased elastic reference value succeeded in invaginating the tissue with various parameters.
source: To validate our new model, we simulated the epithelial cell monolayer with the decreased elastic reference value (Figure 4a, Figure 4—video 1). The inner cells shrank the apical surface simultaneously, and they were deformed into the wedge shape with fluctuating but almost straight lateral surfaces, succeeding in invaginating the tissue with various parameters.
evidence: This describes successful simulation results shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The tissue apical surface was kept relatively flat when the surface elastic modulus was high even though cells adopted wedge shape.
source: Interestingly, the tissue apical surface was kept relatively flat when the surface elastic modulus was high even though the cells adopted the wedge shape (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is an observation from the simulations shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The gradient contractility model enabled cells to shrink apical surface simultaneously, but often some cells shrank faster than neighbors and were delaminated by chance.
source: Even though the gradient contractility enabled the cells to shrink the apical surface simultaneously, often some of the cells shrank faster than neighbors and were delaminated by chance (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes results from testing an alternative model shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The apical constriction model was robust against cell shapes, working with thinner and thicker cells.
source: The apical constriction could bend the tissue with thinner and thicker cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), demonstrating that the model was robust against cell shapes.
evidence: This describes robustness testing results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: When surrounding cells were assigned an affinity to the apical ECM, the invagination was slightly promoted.
source: When the surrounding cells were assigned an affinity to the apical ECM, the cells were spread on the ECM and pushed the center cells toward the midline, and the invagination was slightly promoted (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes simulation results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Tissue invagination was largely promoted by the supracellular myosin cable with a wide range of pulling force and other parameters.
source: Surprisingly, the tissue invagination was largely promoted by the supracellular myosin cable with a wide range of the pulling force and also wide ranges of other parameters.
evidence: This describes simulation results from Figure 5.

claim: Combining both the supracellular myosin cable and the cell surface elasticity made a sharp bending when the pulling force was sufficiently high.
source: However, combining both the supracellular myosin cable and the cell surface elasticity made a sharp bending when the pulling force acting on the adherens junction was sufficiently high.
evidence: This describes a synergistic effect observed in simulations.

claim: During tracheal pit invagination, there was no obvious change in the distribution pattern of cellular junctional tension inside and around the tracheal pit.
source: During the process, there was no obvious change in the distribution pattern of cellular junctional tension inside and around the tracheal pit (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is an observation from the geometrical tension inference shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The apical surface area decreased and the relative pressure increased among the invaginated cells during tracheal pit formation.
source: On the other hand, the apical surface area decreased and the relative pressure increased among the invaginated cells (Figure 6c–e).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis shown in Figure 6c-e.

claim: Variances of the apical area and the relative pressure did not increase during tracheal pit formation, suggesting actual pressure value was increased simultaneously by cell deformation.
source: Note that variances of the apical area and the relative pressure did not increase (Figure 6d and e), suggesting that an actual pressure value was also increased simultaneously by the cell deformation.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 6d and e.

claim: The tracheal pit results were consistent with the model that lateral cell-cell junction was kept straight by increasing but balanced pressure.
source: These results were consistent with our model, indicating that the lateral cell-cell junction of the tracheal pit cell was kept straight by the increasing but balanced pressure.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the experimental observations to the model.

claim: The increased apical surface contractility could not drive apical constriction in the cellular Potts model simulation.
source: In this study, we demonstrated that the increased apical surface contractility could not drive the apical constriction
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding from the simulations.

claim: When cells were assigned high apical surface contractility, cells became rounded and delaminated one by one from edges in the cellular Potts model simulation.
source: When the cells were assigned a high apical surface contractility, the cells became rounded and delaminated one by one from edges in the cellular Potts model simulation.
evidence: This summarizes the simulation results.

claim: The vertex model simulation was substantially affected by the straight lateral surface.
source: However, the vertex model simulation was substantially affected by the straight lateral surface (Figure 3d–f), which was not natural for the epithelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the energy analysis shown in Figure 3d-f.

claim: The difference in simulation results between the models could be due to whether cell rearrangement was included or not.
source: Thus the difference in simulation results between the models could be due to whether the cell rearrangement was included or not.
evidence: This is a speculation about the cause of differences between models.

claim: The cellular Potts model included curved cell surface and cell rearrangement innately, elucidating the importance of those factors.
source: In contrast to the vertex model, the cellular Potts model included the curved cell surface and the cell rearrangement innately, it elucidated the importance of those factors.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantages of the cellular Potts model.

claim: The requirement of simultaneous contraction is consistent with the non-autonomous disruption of apical constriction.
source: For the apical constriction, we considered the modified apical surface elasticity as a plausible underlying mechanism, where the synchronized decrease in cell volume and increase in pressure balances the pressure between the cells and keeps the lateral cell-cell interface straight. The requirement of simultaneous contraction is also consistent with the non-autonomous disruption of apical constriction (Guglielmi et al., 2015; Galea et al., 2021).
evidence: This connects the model predictions to experimental observations with citations.

claim: The cellular Potts model reproduced tissue invagination with a wide range of parameter values, indicating robustness of the model.
source: With the elasticity-based apical constriction model, the cellular Potts model reproduced a tissue invagination. It succeeded with a wide range of parameter values, indicating a robustness of the model.
evidence: This summarizes the simulation results demonstrating model robustness.

claim: The cellular Potts model intrinsically included a high degree of freedom for cell shape, cell rearrangement, and fluctuation, which allowed finding the importance of balanced pressure.
source: That is, we could find the importance of the balanced pressure because the cellular Potts model intrinscally included a high degree of freedom for the cell shape, the cell rearrangement, and the fluctuation.
evidence: This is an inference about why the cellular Potts model revealed new insights.

claim: The tissue apical surface remained relatively flat when cells were assigned higher surface elastic modulus.
source: Interestingly, the tissue apical surface remained relatively flat when the cells were assigned higher surface elastic modulus.
evidence: This is an observation from the simulations.

claim: If the apical myosin would be condensed by the shrinkage of the apical surface, it would increase the apical tension in the shrinking cell and promote cell delamination further.
source: If we presumed that the apical myosin would be condensed by the shrinkage of the apical surface, it would increase the apical tension in the shrinking cell and is expected to promote the cell delamination further.
evidence: This is a speculation about the effect of myosin condensation.

claim: In many epithelial tissues, the apical myosin was found not permanently active but its flow, activation, and resultant apical surface contraction was pulsed, followed by partial relaxation.
source: In many tissues, the apical myosin was found not permanently active but its flow, activation, and resultant apical surface contraction was pulsed, followed by a partial relaxation (Martin et al., 2009; Solon et al., 2009; Martin et al., 2010; Mason et al., 2013; Booth et al., 2014; Kerridge et al., 2016; Mason et al., 2016; Krueger et al., 2020; Martin and Goldstein, 2014; Miao and Blankenship, 2020).
evidence: This describes observed myosin dynamics with multiple citations.

claim: The contraction and partial relaxation is iterated to decrease the apical surface progressively, called ratchet model or ratcheting mechanism.
source: The contraction and partial relaxation is iterated to decrease the apical surface progressively, and it is called ratchet model or ratcheting mechanism.
evidence: This defines a known mechanism in the field.

claim: Some studies pointed out an involvement of endocytosis in the apical constriction and especially in its ratcheting.
source: While it is yet to be clarified how the ratcheting prevents the apical surface from expanding back to its original width during the relaxation, some studies pointed out an involvement of the endocytosis in the apical constriction (Lee and Harland, 2010; Mateus et al., 2011; Ossipova et al., 2014; Ossipova et al., 2015; Le and Chung, 2021), and especially in its ratcheting (Miao et al., 2019; Kowalczyk et al., 2021; Chen and He, 2022).
evidence: This references studies on endocytosis involvement with citations.

claim: When apical endocytosis was impaired but myosin activity was retained, cells exhibited pulsed apical contraction but fully turned back to their original shape in the following relaxation.
source: When the apical endocytosis was impaired but the myosin activity was retained, cells exhibited the pulsed apical contraction but fully turned back to their original shape in the following relaxation.
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Miao et al., 2019 downregulated endocytosis in a Drosophila gastrula and observed apical contraction in the edge cells of a mesoderm.
source: Interestingly, Miao et al., 2019 downregulated endocytosis in a Drosophila gastrula and observed the apical contraction in the edge cells of a mesoderm which would be invaginated by the apical constriction in the wild type embryo.
evidence: This describes a specific experimental result with citation.

claim: The edge-specific contraction observed by Miao et al., 2019 resembles the result of simulations with increased apical surface contractility.
source: This edge-specific contraction resembles the result of simulations with the increased apical surface contractility (Figure 2)
evidence: This connects experimental observations to simulation results.

claim: Most preceding studies supposed that endocytosis regulated ratcheting indirectly by facilitating apical actomyosin network remodeling.
source: Although most of the preceding studies supposed that the endocytosis regulated the ratcheting indirectly by facilitating apical actomyosin network remodeling, here we would propose that the cell membrane itself increases the apical surface tension by changing the reference value.
evidence: This contrasts the authors' proposal with existing interpretations.

claim: The cell membrane bears surface tension when extended, and the surface tension magnitude is proportional to the change from the reference value.
source: Since the cell membrane is an elastic sheet, it bears the surface tension when extended, and the surface tension magnitude is proportional to the change from the reference value.
evidence: This describes a physical property of cell membranes.

claim: The reference value of cell membrane is an area when the membrane is not stretched nor compressed, and it can be decreased by endocytosis.
source: The reference value is an area of the membrane when the membrane is not stretched nor compressed, and it can be decreased by the endocytosis.
evidence: This proposes how endocytosis affects membrane properties.

claim: Actin filament linker βH-spectrin was reported regulating the ratcheting.
source: It might be also possible that the remodeling of the apical actomyosin ratchets the relaxation, as actin filament linker βH-spectrin was also reported regulating the ratcheting (Krueger et al., 2020).
evidence: This references an alternative mechanism with citation.

claim: The authors propose a four-step model: (1) actomyosin generates pulsed contractility contracting the apical surface temporally; (2) the contraction will be fully relaxed without endocytosis; (3) endocytosis decreases the reference value of apical surface elasticity during pulsed contraction; and (4) after pulsed contraction and endocytosis, the cell apical surface is partially relaxed.
source: In summary, we propose that (1) the actomyosin generates pulsed contractility, and the cell apical surface is contracted temporally; (2) the contraction will be fully relaxed without the endocytosis; (3) the endocytosis decreases the reference value of the apical surface elasticity during the pulsed contraction; and (4) after the pulsed contraction and endocytosis, the cell apical surface is partially relaxed (Figure 7a).
evidence: This is the authors' proposed model illustrated in Figure 7a.

claim: When the apical myosin is constantly active, the increased contractility is balanced among cells and makes edge cells delaminated.
source: When the apical myosin is constantly active as in the conventional model, the increased contractility is balanced among the cells and makes the edge cells delaminated (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model illustrated in Figure 7b.

claim: When myosin activity is pulsed and sporadic but not accompanied by surface elasticity modification, the temporal contraction is fully relaxed and the tissue remains in the same shape.
source: When the myosin activity is pulsed and sporadic but not accompanied by the surface elasticity modification, the temporal contraction is fully relaxed and the tissue remains in the same shape (Figure 7c).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model illustrated in Figure 7c.

claim: When sporadic pulse of myosin activation is followed by endocytosis, cells undergo simultaneous apical contraction, pressure is balanced among cells, keeping the lateral cell-cell junction straight and deforming cells into wedge shape.
source: When the sporadic pulse of myosin activation is followed by the endocytosis, the cells undergo the simultaneous apical contraction, and then the pressure is balanced among the cells, keeping the cell lateral cell-cell junction straight and deforming the cells into the wedge shape (Figure 7d).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model illustrated in Figure 7d.

claim: It may be possible that myosin activation is not patterned but pulsed across the entire tissue, while endocytosis is patterned, and the tissue will be bent at the site of increased endocytotic activity.
source: In the actual tissue, the apical localization of the myosin and regulators of the endocytosis were both patterned. However, it may be possible in theory that the myosin activation is not patterned but is pulsed across the entire tissue, while the endocytosis is patterned, and the tissue will be bent at the site of the increased endocytotic activity (Figure 7e).
evidence: This is a theoretical possibility illustrated in Figure 7e.

claim: Too high myosin activation would prevent apical constriction by keeping the apical surface flat.
source: Another interesting notion was that too high myosin activation would prevent the apical constriction. Even if the apical contraction is synchronized and the lateral surface is kept straight so that the cells are deformed into the wedge shape, the too high apical surface tension will try to make the apical surface as short as possible, and the apical surface will be kept flat (Figure 7f).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model illustrated in Figure 7f.

claim: Mechanisms that do not generate apical surface tension, such as zippering or supracellular myosin cable, may promote deep invagination.
source: On the other hand, mechanisms which does not generate the apical surface tension, such like the zippering (Bahri et al., 2010; Hashimoto et al., 2015; Galea et al., 2017) or the supracellular myosin cable encircling the contracting cells (Nishimura et al., 2007; Röper, 2012; Chung et al., 2017), may promote the deep invagination.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model with citations to relevant mechanisms.

claim: The supracellular contractile ring alone could not drive tissue invagination.
source: Note that we also demonstrated that the supracellular contractile ring alone could not drive the tissue invagination (Figure 2c).
evidence: This references a simulation result shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The simulation results were consistent with studies of endocytosis in apical constriction and suggested why and how endocytosis and ratcheting was required for apical constriction.
source: In conclusion, we elucidated how distinctively the surface contractility and the surface elasticity would regulate tissue morphogenesis. Our simulation results were consistent with the studies of the endocytosis in apical constriction, and suggested why and how the endocytosis and the ratcheting was required for the apical constriction.
evidence: This is a summary of the main conclusions.
